syllabus_name: GenAI Project_Dự án TTNT tạo sinh
description:
This capstone project course is designed to consolidate and apply students' knowledge in generative AI and large language models through a substantial team project. Students scope, design, build, evaluate, and present a non-trivial generative AI system or empirical study. Topics applied include:
- The application of generative AI techniques (LLMs, diffusion, RAG, agents, fine-tuning) to solve practical problems.
- The identification and adaptation of generative AI methodologies from current research for specific use cases.
- The development of a comprehensive solution approach using prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation, fine-tuning (LoRA / QLoRA), or agent design.
- The evaluation and analysis of generative outputs using appropriate metrics (perplexity, ROUGE, faithfulness, FID, human / LLM-as-judge protocols) and rigorous failure-mode analysis.
- Recognition of appropriate scenarios for prompting vs RAG vs fine-tuning vs agent design.
- Selection of suitable metrics and benchmarks for generative-system evaluation.
- Understanding the ethical, safety, provenance, and legal implications of generative AI (hallucination, bias, deepfakes, copyright, content provenance / C2PA).
- Implementation and reflection on generative pipelines including data preparation, model adaptation, inference / serving, and post-deployment monitoring.
- Effective teamwork and project management across a multi-phase delivery.
tools:
- Programming Languages: Python 3.10+
- Software Tools: Jupyter Notebook / Google Colab, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, Diffusers, PEFT, TRL, LangChain, vLLM
- Models: Hosted frontier APIs (Claude, GPT, Gemini) and open-weight families (Llama, Mistral, Qwen, DeepSeek)
- Datasets: Hugging Face Datasets, Kaggle, publicly licensed corpora
- Additional Resources: Papers with Code, arXiv, GitHub, Hugging Face Hub, Weights & Biases for experiment tracking
